title: Weekly regression roundup: onboarding evals & action items
summary: This is the weekly regression roundup for the current model onboarding cohort (candidate = rdm-model-2.1.0). Focus: prompt-set stability, top failure modes across onboarding suites, a short root-cause hypothesis list, and concrete action items for next sprint. Canary traffic is running (5% to candidate) — this report integrates canary logs + offline evals (customer_faq_v2, billing_parsing, summarization_long, code_gen_smoke).
metrics:
High-level deltas (candidate rdm-model-2.1.0 vs baseline rdm-model-2.0.4 over the last 7 days):
- Mean semantic-accuracy (human-proxy): 0.842 -> 0.802 (drop 4.0 percentage points absolute)
- Hallucination indicator (auto heuristic): 12.4 / 1k -> 18.7 / 1k (increase +6.3 / 1k)
- Safety flag rate (auto): 3.1 / 1k -> 5.4 / 1k (increase +2.3 / 1k)
- Token-latency P95: 120ms -> 118ms (slight improvement)
- Canary error rate (5% traffic): 0.9% -> 1.3% (+0.4pp)
Notes: most quality regressions concentrated in billing_parsing and summarization_long prompt sets. Latency/throughput unaffected in dedicated infra tests.
top_failures:
Top failure clusters observed (ranked by impact * frequency):
1) Billing parsing: numeric extraction errors and missed currency context (impact: billing automations fail). Example prompt: "Extract the amount and currency from: 'Invoice #3342 — USD1,200.00 due 2025-12-01'" -> candidate returns '1200' without currency tag, baseline returned 'USD 1,200.00'.
2) Long summarization hallucinations: invented clauses in contract summaries for >1500 token inputs. Example: input paragraph referencing 'Section 3.4' — candidate fabricates a remediation step.
3) Code generation edge-case: incorrect type inference for small JS snippets (smoke tests show intermittent failures where baseline passed).
4) FAQ factual regression: candidate misses product-specific facts in customer_faq_v2 (3 specific KB items).
5) Safety false positives: auto-safety pipeline marking benign admin texts as sensitive at higher rate (affects throughput of moderation queue).
prompt_sets_notes:
Prompt-set snapshots used this week: customer_faq_v2 (480 prompts), billing_parsing (220 prompts), summarization_long (150 prompts with >1k tokens), code_gen_smoke (120 unit prompts).
Changes since last snapshot: customer_faq_v2 added 42 new API-related questions (JIRA: ML-1012). billing_parsing introduced two currency formats (₩ and INR with trailing text) which may have exposed tokenization-related behavior in the candidate. summarization_long includes 12 legal docs added by SolutionsEng for private-deploy tests.
Quick wins: add explicit currency-tagging prompts to billing_parsing; include more negative examples for hallucination detection in summarization_long.
regression_analysis:
Preliminary hypotheses (ranked):
- Tokenization difference: candidate's new tokenizer merging numeric+symbol tokens leading to currency label loss in billing_parsing. Evidence: failure cases align with non-ASCII currency glyphs and group separators.
- Context window handling: candidate's attention-kernel change increases propensity to attend to lead sentences and ignore appendices in long docs, correlating with hallucinations in summarization_long.
- Safety classifier calibration drift: candidate model's score distribution shifted; auto-thresholds need recalibration.
Data quality notes: 6% of the failing billing_parsing prompts contain OCR artifacts from customer samples — need filtration.
Requested offline tests: run targeted tokenization unit tests (see linked PR) and rerun summarization_long with forced-attention ablations.
